FIBA Basketball World Cup team|Team]]}} }} '''Derrick Martell Rose''' (born October 4, 1988) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played one year of [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]] before being drafted [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall]] by his hometown [[Chicago Bulls]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=Bulls go with native Chicagoan Rose over Beasley|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2008/news/story?id=3462594|work=ESPN|date=June 26, 2008|access-date=June 26, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151030225012/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2008/news/story?id=3462594|archive-date=October 30, 2015|url-status=live}} Nicknamed "'''D-Rose'''", and sometimes referred to as "'''the Windy City Assassin'''" or "'''Pooh'''",{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Jones|title=Best Nickname from Every NBA Team |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1015781-best-nickname-from-every-nba-team|work=Bleacher Report|date=January 12, 2012|access-date=November 27, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128224428/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1015781-best-nickname-from-every-nba-team|archive-date=November 28, 2023|url-status=live}} he was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] in 2009 and became the youngest player to win the [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award]] in 2011 at the age of 22 years and 7 months. Rose was born and raised in Chicago, and attended [[Simeon Career Academy]]. He was highly recruited by colleges, eventually choosing to join the [[University of Memphis]] under coach [[John Calipari]]. Rose led the Tigers to the most wins in NCAA history (a 38–2 record), their first number 1 ranking in 25 years, and an appearance in the NCAA championship game. In 2009, an NCAA investigation revealed that Rose's [[SAT]] scores had been invalidated, and as a result, the NCAA vacated Memphis' entire [[2007–08 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|2007–08 season]].{{cite news|first=Marlen|last=Garci|title=NCAA vacates Memphis' '07–08 season record, Final Four run|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/2009-08-20-memphis-ncaa-penalties_N.htm|work=USA Today|date=August 19, 2009|access-date=August 20, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111212010354/http://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/2009-08-20-memphis-ncaa-penalties_N.htm|archive-date=December 12, 2011|url-status=live}} Rose struggled with significant knee injuries throughout his career. In the first round of the [[2012 NBA playoffs]] against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], Rose tore his [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|ACL]] in his left knee. He required surgery and was subsequently sidelined for the entire 2012–13 season.{{cite web|title=Chicago Bulls Derrick Rose getting knee examined by Dr. James Andrews|url=https://www.espn.com/chicago/nba/story/_/id/8074004/chicago-bulls-derrick-rose-getting-knee-examined-dr-james-andrews|work=ESPN|date=June 19, 2012|access-date=June 20, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120620020842/http://espn.go.com/chicago/nba/story/_/id/8074004/chicago-bulls-derrick-rose-getting-knee-examined-dr-james-andrews|archive-date=June 20, 2012|url-status=live}} Rose returned to play in 2013–14, but in November 2013, he injured his right meniscus, causing him to miss the remainder of the season.{{cite web|title=Bulls' Rose is likely out for season|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2013/11/25/bulls-rose-is-likely-out-for-season/|website=ChicagoTribune.com|date=November 25, 2013|access-date=November 6, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106090742/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-11-25/sports/chi-derrick-rose-surgery-20131124_1_derrick-rose-tom-thibodeau-chicago-bulls|archive-date=November 6, 2014|url-status=live}} He returned once again the following season, but knee injuries continued to impact his availability and production. In June 2016, Rose was traded to the [[New York Knicks]], where he finished the final year of his contract. He signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on a minimum salary for the 2017–18 season but was hobbled by ankle injuries, which led to him being traded to, and subsequently waived by, the [[Utah Jazz]] in February 2018.{{cite news|title=Jazz waive Derrick Rose after acquisition from Cavaliers|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/jazz-waive-derrick-rose-acquisition-cavaliers/|work=Sportsnet|date=February 10, 2018|access-date=June 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210604003459/https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/jazz-waive-derrick-rose-acquisition-cavaliers/|archive-date=June 4, 2021|url-status=live}} He signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] a month later on a rest-of-season contract; he stayed with the team through the following season and enjoyed a revived role as a [[sixth man]]. For the 2019–20 season, the [[Detroit Pistons]] signed Rose to his first non-minimum salary contract since 2017, and he continued to be successful off the bench.{{cite news|first=Mark|last=Schanowski|title=NBA power rankings: Derrick Rose's career renaissance continues in Detroit|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba-power-rankings-derrick-roses-050447872.html|work=NBC Sports|date=December 16, 2019|access-date=June 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220408145742/https://sports.yahoo.com/nba-power-rankings-derrick-roses-050447872.html|archive-date=April 8, 2022|url-status=dead}} The following season, he was reunited with his former coach [[Tom Thibodeau]] when the Knicks re-acquired him in a trade. In July 2023, Rose signed for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in free agency. In September 2024, Rose was released by the Grizzlies, and subsequently announced his retirement. ==Early life== Rose was born on [[Chicago's South Side|Chicago’s South Side]] and grew up in the [[Englewood, Chicago|Englewood]] neighborhood.{{cite web|last1=Jensen|first1=Sean|title=Derrick Rose keeps tough Englewood area close to his heart|url=http://www.suntimes.com/sports/basketball/5365750-419/derrick-rose-stays-connected-to-tough-englewood-neighborhood.html|website=Chicago Sun-Times|access-date=August 4, 2014|date=May 14, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808055234/http://www.suntimes.com/sports/basketball/5365750-419/derrick-rose-stays-connected-to-tough-englewood-neighborhood.html|archive-date=August 8, 2014|url-status=dead}} He is the youngest son of Brenda Rose after Dwayne, Reggie, and Allan. All three were talented basketball players who taught Rose the ins and outs of basketball on nearby courts.{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1114058/index.htm|title=The Well-guarded Guard|access-date=May 12, 2011|archive-date=October 11, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111011085004/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1114058/index.htm|url-status=dead}} As his talent for the sport grew, Rose began to attract outside attention, leading his mother and brothers to restrict outside contact to him. His mother feared he would be exploited and have his path to the NBA diverted by outside parties like street agents, similar to what happened to former Chicago prospect [[Ronnie Fields]].{{cite magazine |url=http://www.sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/highschool/11/20/hs.rose1127/1.html |title=The Well-Guarded Guard |author=George Dohrmann |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=November 21, 2006 |access-date=December 26, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090123224700/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/highschool/11/20/hs.rose1127/1.html |archive-date=January 23, 2009 |url-status=dead }} ==High school career== By the time Rose enrolled at [[Simeon Career Academy]] in 2003, he was widely noticed by collegiate coaches. Despite his reputation, he played freshmen and JV basketball for the Wolverines. He wore No. 25 in honor of [[Ben Wilson (basketball)|Ben "Benji" Wilson]], a promising player who was murdered by a gang member during his senior year in 1984.{{cite web |url=http://www.sports.espn.go.com/espn/page2/story?page=jackson/080701&sportCat=nba |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001103953/http://sports.espn.go.com/espn/page2/story?page=jackson/080701&sportCat=nba |url-status=dead |archive-date= 2015-10-01|title=Spirit of former Chicago high school star lives on in Rose |author=Scoop Jackson |work=ESPN.com |date=July 1, 2008 |access-date=January 29, 2009 }} Rose was not allowed on varsity due to a long-standing tradition that head coach Bob Hambric, who had been with the school since 1980 had no freshmen on the varsity team. That rule did not lessen Rose's play, and he went on to put up 18.5 [[Point (basketball)|points]], 6.6 [[Assist (basketball)|assist]]s, 4.7 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s and 2.1 [[Steal (basketball)|steal]]s per game and led both the freshmen and sophomores to city championships with a 24–1 record.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/derrick_rose.html |title=2008 NBA Draft Player Profile : : Derrick Rose |work=Bulls.com |access-date=December 10, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111217234316/http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/derrick_rose.html |archive-date=December 17, 2011 |url-status=dead }} Hambric softened his stance and allowed the freshman a chance to play on varsity in the state tournament, but Rose declined, wanting the players to get due credit.{{cite web |url=http://preps.scout.com/2/493015.html |title=Believe The Hype |author=Jon Mahoney |work=Scout |date=January 25, 2005 |access-date=December 27, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081229202544/http://preps.scout.com/2/493015.html |archive-date=December 29, 2008 |url-status=dead }} The next year Hambric retired and Robert Smith was hired, opening the path to varsity. In Rose's debut, he had 22 points, 7 rebounds and 5 steals over [[Thornwood High School]] in a sold-out game filled with college scouts and coaches.{{cite news |url=http://yourseason.suntimes.com/1026724,062608rosedebut.article |title=Flashback: Rose's debut |author=Michael O'Brien |work=Chicago Sun-Times |date=June 30, 2008 |access-date=December 27, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081229202331/http://yourseason.suntimes.com/1026724,062608rosedebut.article |archive-date=December 29, 2008 |url-status=dead }} He led the Wolverines to a 30–5 mark while averaging 19.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, 8.3 assists and 2.4 steals but the season ended after a loss in state regionals. Rose's play garnered him his first national award: a [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] third team spot.{{cite web |url=http://www.parade.com/articles/editions/2005/edition_04-03-2005/featured_2 |title=Meet PARADE's All-America... Team |access-date=January 1, 2008 |author=Michael O'Shea |work=Parade.com |date=April 3, 2005 |archive-date=January 10, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100110055044/http://www.parade.com/articles/editions/2005/edition_04-03-2005/featured_2 |url-status=live }} During Rose's junior year in 2006, the Simeon Wolverines broke through and won the [[Chicago Public High School League|Chicago Public League]] championship held at the [[United Center]], where Rose starred with 25 points and crowd pleasing dunks. The team advanced through the playoffs and earned a berth in the Class AA state championship against [[Richwoods High School]], where a fourth quarter [[buzzer beater]] by Richwood forced overtime. The score was knotted at 29 late in the extra period when Rose stole the ball and buried the game winning jumper as time expired, giving Simeon its first state title since the Wilson-led Wolverines won in 1984. The team finished 33–4 and ranked nationally,{{cite magazine |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/highschool/04/07/hoops.rankings2/ |title=Final Top 25 Poll |author=Jon Mahoney |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=April 6, 2006 |access-date=March 29, 2009 |archive-date=November 3, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103194321/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/highschool/04/07/hoops.rankings2/ |url-status=dead }} and Rose was awarded with an All-State Illinois mention, [[EA Sports]] All-American Second Team pick{{cite web |work=Rivals.com |url=http://ssbasketball.rivals.com/content.asp?SID=1132&CID=537673 |title=2006 EA SPORTS Boys All American Team |access-date=December 25, 2008 |archive-date=February 22, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120222080723/http://ssbasketball.rivals.com/content.asp?SID=1132&CID=537673 |url-status=dead }} and another ''Parade'' All-American selection.{{cite magazine |magazine=Parade Magazine |url=http://all-americans.parade.com/2006_boy_basketball/2006_boys_basketball.html |title=All-America Teams |access-date=December 25, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090212130829/http://all-americans.parade.com/2006_boy_basketball/2006_boys_basketball.html |archive-date=February 12, 2009 }} Entering his senior year, Rose was ranked the fifth best prospect in the nation by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''. Rose averaged 19.7 points on 47.5% shooting, 6.3 assists and 4.9 rebounds per game in his first playoff series, as the Bulls were defeated by the Celtics in seven games.nba.com, [http://www.nba.com/playerfile/derrick_rose/career_stats.html Derrick Rose Career Stats Page] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120530005556/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/derrick_rose/career_stats.html |date=May 30, 2012 }}, accessed October 29, 2009. ====2009–10 season: First All-Star selection==== Rose's sophomore season started off with an ankle injury in his first preseason game. Rose would go on to miss the rest of the preseason. Rose started the Bulls' season opener against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] but played limited minutes. Rose's ankle bothered him for most of November, but as his ankle healed, his game improved. On January 16, 2010, against the [[Washington Wizards]], Rose recorded 37 points, including a layup to win the game 121–119 with 5.4 seconds to go in the second overtime.{{Cite web |date=16 January 2010 |title=Rose's 37 points help Bulls escape Wizards in double overtime |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/300115004 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=December 6, 2023 |archive-date=December 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207180535/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/300115004 |url-status=dead }} On January 28, Rose was elected to his first career [[2010 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Game]] as a reserve for the Eastern Conference, making him the first Bulls player to be selected since [[Michael Jordan]] in 1998.[https://www.espn.com/chicago/nba/news/story?id=4867386 Bulls' Rose selected to All-Star team], accessed January 28, 2010. Rose ended up with eight points, four assists and three steals in the game. On April 13, 2010, Rose scored 39 points against the Boston Celtics, making 15–22 field goals and 9–10 free throws. The Bulls once again made the playoffs in the 2009–10 season, finishing with a 41–41 record. In the playoffs Rose averaged 26.8 points and 7.2 assists, but the Bulls lost in five games to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/derrick_rose/index.html|title=Official NBA bio of Derrick Rose - NBA.com|website=[[NBA.com]]|access-date=March 24, 2009|archive-date=March 1, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110301174050/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/derrick_rose/index.html|url-status=live}} ====2010–11 season: MVP season==== [[File:Derrick Rose 2.jpg|thumb|right|Rose led the Bulls to 62 wins, and the best record overall, during the 2010–11 NBA season.]] On October 30, 2010, in the Bulls' second game of the season, Rose scored 39 points in a 101–91 win against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. Two days after, Rose contributed 13 assists, helping [[Luol Deng]] score a career-high 40 points in a win against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. On December 10, Rose scored 29 points and had 9 assists, leading the Bulls to their first victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] since December 19, 2006. On January 16, 2011, Rose outdueled fellow Chicago native [[Dwyane Wade]] in a 99–96 win over the [[Miami Heat]], scoring 34 points, of which 11 in the fourth quarter.{{Cite web |date=16 January 2011 |title=Bulls send LeBron James-less Heat to 3rd straight loss; Chris Bosh hurt |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/310115004 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=December 6, 2023 |archive-date=December 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207180644/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/310115004 |url-status=dead }} On January 17, he recorded his first career [[triple-double]] with 22 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists in a 96–84 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20110117/CHIMEM/gameinfo.html|title=Bulls at Grizzlies|website=[[NBA.com]]|access-date=May 29, 2011|archive-date=March 10, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110310061143/http://www.nba.com/games/20110117/CHIMEM/gameinfo.html|url-status=live}} On January 27, Rose was announced as a starting guard on the [[2011 NBA All-Star Game|2011 NBA All-Star Team]] for the East squad.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/allstar/2011/|title=NBA.com - 2011 All-Star Events|website=www.nba.com|access-date=January 28, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110221215029/http://www.nba.com/allstar/2011/|archive-date=February 21, 2011|url-status=dead}} On February 17, in the Bulls' last game before the All-Star break, Rose set a career-high with 42 points, while also recording 8 assists and 5 rebounds, as the Bulls beat the [[San Antonio Spurs]] 109–99. On March 19, he equalled that tally in a 115–108 overtime loss by the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |date=19 March 2011 |title=Tyler Hansbrough, Pacers thwart Derrick Rose-led rally, end Bulls' win streak at 8 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/310318011 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=December 6, 2023 |archive-date=December 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207180920/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/310318011 |url-status=dead }} The loss was only one of two that the Bulls suffered in the last 23 games of the season. On March 26, Rose had a career-high 17 assists, along with 30 points, in a 95–87 victory over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. On April 10, Rose scored 39 points on 13-of-17 shooting in a 102–99 win over the [[Orlando Magic]], in one of the final regular season matches of the season which saw the Bulls go undefeated in the month of April. On April 13, Rose put on a show at the [[Madison Square Garden]] with 26 points, shooting 10-of-19 and throwing down several crowd-pleasing dunks in a 103–90 win over the Knicks, leading coach [[Mike D'Antoni]] to compliment him in the post-game interview: "His athletic ability is ridiculous. He's come farther, quicker, faster than anyone expected; he's playing at a level that not many people play."{{Cite web |date=13 April 2011 |title=Bulls rout Knicks after leaping out to 26-2 run to start second half |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/310412018 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=December 6, 2023 |archive-date=December 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207180533/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/310412018 |url-status=dead }} At the end of the [[2010–11 NBA season]] the Bulls finished with a league leading record of 62–20.{{cite news|title=NBA Standings – 2010–11|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/standings/_/year/2011/seasontype/2|newspaper=ESPN|access-date=December 19, 2011|archive-date=December 17, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111217010101/http://espn.go.com/nba/standings/_/year/2011/seasontype/2|url-status=live}} Their 60+ wins was the Bulls' first such season since [[1997–98 NBA season|1997–98]] and sixth 60+ win in franchise history.{{cite news|title=Chicago Bulls Power Rankings – 2010–11|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/standings/_/year/2011/seasontype/2|newspaper=ESPN|access-date=December 19, 2011|archive-date=December 17, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111217010101/http://espn.go.com/nba/standings/_/year/2011/seasontype/2|url-status=live}} At season's end, Rose became only the third player since the [[1972–73 NBA season]] to record 2,000 points and 600 assists in a single season. The other two players were [[LeBron James]] and [[Michael Jordan]].{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/654658-derrick-rose-the-surprisingly-historic-numbers-of-his-mvp-seeason|title=Derrick Rose: The Surprisingly Historic Numbers of His MVP Season|first=Kelly|last=Scaletta|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|access-date=April 22, 2011|archive-date=April 11, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110411134318/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/654658-derrick-rose-the-surprisingly-historic-numbers-of-his-mvp-seeason|url-status=live}} On May 3, Rose was named the [[NBA Most Valuable Player]], joining Jordan as the only players to receive the award in Chicago Bulls history.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2011/news/05/03/mvp-award/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt1|title=Chicago's Derrick Rose Wins 2010–11 Kia NBA MVP Award|work=NBA.com|access-date=May 3, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110505081553/http://www.nba.com/2011/news/05/03/mvp-award/index.html?ls=iref%3Anbahpt1|archive-date=May 5, 2011}} At 22 years and 6 months old, Rose also became the youngest player to receive the award ([[Wes Unseld]], formerly the youngest MVP, won the award in 1968–69 at age 23 years, 2 months). In the 2011 NBA playoffs, the Bulls defeated the [[2010–11 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]] and [[2010–11 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]] in the first two rounds. In the Eastern Conference Finals, the Bulls faced the [[2010–11 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]], led by James, [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[Chris Bosh]]. The Bulls lost the series in five games. He had a slow start but scored his first point in the first quarter. He finished the game with 13 points in 20 minutes of play.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/chicago/nba/story/_/id/9778651/derrick-rose-returns-chicago-bulls-first-knee-injury|title=Derrick Rose agrressive in return|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|access-date=October 6, 2013|date=October 5, 2013|first=Nick|last=Friedell|archive-date=October 6, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131006145752/http://espn.go.com/chicago/nba/story/_/id/9778651/derrick-rose-returns-chicago-bulls-first-knee-injury|url-status=live}} On October 16, 2013, Rose returned to play in Chicago for the first time, scoring 22 points against the [[2013–14 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]].
